Curated septal-synthase function and verified E. coli protein membership; WP5060 names FtsW and FtsI.
link.label: Peptidoglycan cytoplasmic synthesis and recycling pathways
link.scope_note: The E. coli exemplar uses FtsW-FtsI for septal peptidoglycan synthesis. The link covers this segment of WP5060, not every cytoplasmic or recycling reaction and not archaeal FtsZ division.

evidence.notes: Mercer and Weiss 2002 show that E. coli FtsW recruits FtsI to division sites and connects this complex to septal peptidoglycan synthesis. Abstract read through Europe PMC on 2026-10-05.

link.basis: The curated sidewall-synthesis function overlaps the peptidoglycan output of WP5060; this is not an exact shared-accession join.
link.label: Peptidoglycan cytoplasmic synthesis and recycling pathways
link.scope_note: This refers to sidewall peptidoglycan synthesis in the E. coli exemplar. It does not identify the elongasome with the whole WP5060 pathway or equate the reviewed K-12 PBP2 accession with the separate species-level entry in WP5060.

evidence.notes: Typas et al. 2011 review peptidoglycan synthesis complexes and cytoskeletal control of sacculus growth; the existing sidewall-synthesis function provides the structure-specific context. Abstract read through Europe PMC on 2026-10-05.

link.basis: WP5060 contains a Peptidoglycan Layer product; the structure record describes the E. coli sacculus.
link.label: Peptidoglycan cytoplasmic synthesis and recycling pathways
link.scope_note: The E. coli peptidoglycan sacculus is related to the peptidoglycan material produced in WP5060. This is a material-production relation, not equivalence to the entire pathway or a claim about every bacterial wall.

evidence.notes: Vollmer et al. 2008 describe the peptidoglycan sacculus as cross-linked glycan strands forming the bacterial cell-wall structure. Abstract read through Europe PMC on 2026-10-05.
